Surat Ha Mim as-Sajdah (Fussilat): Makkiyyah. It has fifty-four verses, seven hundred and ninety-six words, and three thousand three hundred and fifty letters.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ha Mim. ﴿A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, a Book whose verses are distinguished, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know.﴾ And had it been non-Arabic, they would not have understood it.

Regarding the case-ending (naṣb) of "al-Qur'an," there are several views:

The first: the verb has been occupied by the signs, so that they have become like the subject, and the "al-Qur'an" is put in the accusative because the clarifying falls upon it.

The second: it is in the accusative of praise.

The third: it is in the accusative by repetition of the verb, meaning "We distinguished a Qur'an."

The fourth: it is in the accusative by supposing a verb, meaning "We mention a Qur'an."

The fifth: it is in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl).

The sixth: it is in the accusative of separation (qaṭʿ).

﴿Bringing good news and warning﴾: two attributes of the Qur'an. ﴿But most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾, meaning they do not hear it and do not give ear to it. ﴿And they say: "Our hearts are in coverings (akinnah) from what you call us to, and in our ears is a deafness, and between us and you is a barrier."﴾ The people meant are the polytheists of Makkah. "Coverings" means veils: ﴿from what you call us to﴾, so we do not understand what he says. Mujahid said: like a quiver for arrows. ﴿And in our ears is a deafness﴾, so we do not hear what he says. They said this only to make him despair of their accepting his religion, and it is by way of metaphor. ﴿And between us and you is a barrier﴾: a difference in religion, so their disagreement became a screen and a barrier, so that they do not gather, do not agree because of it, and do not see one another. ﴿So act﴾ according to what your religion requires. ﴿Indeed, we are acting﴾ according to what our religion requires. Muqatil said: so you worship your god, and we worship our gods.

﴿Say: "I am only a human like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God. So take a straight course toward Him and seek His forgiveness."﴾ Al-Hasan said: Allah taught him humility. ﴿Take a straight course toward Him﴾: turn your faces toward Him in obedience and sincerity. ﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾ for your sins that have passed. ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakah﴾. Ibn Abbas said: they do not testify that there is no god but Allah, and this is the zakah of the souls. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: they do not acknowledge zakah, nor believe in it, nor regard giving it as obligatory. Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: they do not give charity and do not spend in obedience.

It used to be said: zakah is the bridge of Islam; whoever crosses it is saved, and whoever stays behind it is destroyed. The people of apostasy after the Prophet (ﷺ) said: as for the prayer, we will pray; as for the zakah, by Allah, we will not let our wealth be seized.

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By Allah, I will not distinguish between things that Allah the Exalted has joined together. By Allah, if they withheld from me a cord (ʿiqal) of what Allah and His Messenger imposed, I would fight them over it."

Mujahid and al-Rabi' said: it means they do not purify their deeds. Al-Farra' said: Quraysh used to feed the pilgrims, so they forbade that to whoever believed in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that is never cut off.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: uncut. Muqatil: not diminished, and from it comes "al-Mann," because a person is diminished by it, that is, his strength. Mujahid: not reckoned. It is also said: not reckoned against them. Al-Suddi said: this verse was revealed concerning the sick, the disabled and the aged who are unable to obey; a reward is written for them as the best of what they used to do when they were healthy. [[Fath al-Qadir: 4/506.]]

﴿Say: "Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿And He placed firm mountains upon it, and blessed it﴾, meaning the earth, by what He created in it of benefits. Al-Suddi said: He made its trees grow. ﴿And measured therein its sustenance﴾. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: meaning the provisions of its people and their livelihoods and what sustains them. Mujahid and Qatadah said: He created in it its seas, its rivers, its trees, and its animals, on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ibn Najih related from Mujahid that he said: it is the rain.

Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: He measured in each land within it what He did not place in the other, so that some of them might live from others through trade from land to land. Thus the Sabiri cloth is from Sabur, the tayalisah (shawls) from al-Ray, the ḥabar and the Yemeni cloth from Yemen. This is the narration of Husayn from Mujahid.

Hayyan related from al-Kalbi, who said: bread is for the people of one region, dates for the people of one region, maize for the people of one region, fish for the people of one region, and likewise its counterparts.

﴿In four days﴾: meaning that this together with the first makes four days, as one says: "I married a woman yesterday and two today," and one of them is the one he married yesterday. It is also said: "I came to Wasit in five and to Basra in ten," so the five are part of the ten. Allah the Exalted thus returned the second to the first and summarized it in mention.

﴿Equal﴾: Abu Ja'far put it in the nominative as a beginning, meaning "it is equal." Al-Hasan and Ya'qub put it in the genitive as an attribute of ﴿in four days﴾; the rest put it in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning "they were equalised in equal measure." It is also said it is in the accusative of circumstance and separation. The meaning of the verse: ﴿equal for those who ask﴾ about that. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: for whoever asked about it, so the matter is thus. It is also said: for those who ask Allah for their needs.

Ibn Zayd said: He decreed that in accordance with their questions, for nothing from their questions occurs except that He knew it before it came to be.

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the meaning is "equal for those who ask and those who do not ask," that is, He made clear the matter of the creation of the earth and what is in it to the one who asks and the one who does not, and He gives to the one who asks and the one who does not.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾: that is, He set out to create the heaven and aimed at its formation. Istiwa' is among the attributes of acts according to most opinions, and this is indicated by His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke﴾, vapor of water. ﴿And He said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or by compulsion."﴾ That is, come with what I created in you of benefits, and bring forth, and manifest yourselves with the interests of My creation. Ibn Abbas said: Allah the Exalted said to the heavens: "Rise with your sun, your moon and your stars," and He said to the earth: "Split open your rivers and bring forth your fruits."

﴿They both said: "We come willingly."﴾ He did not say "willingly" in the feminine dual, because He went with it to the heavens and the earth and those within them; its meaning: "We come with those in us, willingly." When He described them by speech, He treated them in the plural as those who understand. It has reached us that one of the prophets said: "O Lord, if the heavens and the earth, when You said to them, 'Come willingly or by compulsion,' had disobeyed You, what would You have done with them?" He said: "I would command one of My creatures, and it would swallow them." He said: "And where is that creature?" He said: "In a meadow of My meadows." He said: "And where is that meadow?" He said: "In the knowledge of My knowledge."

Ibn Abbas recited: ātiyā and ātainā with the long vowel, meaning: "Give obedience from yourselves." They both said: "We have given."

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By Allah, I will not distinguish between things that Allah the Exalted has joined together. By Allah, if they withheld from me a cord (ʿiqal) of what Allah and His Messenger imposed, I would fight them over it."

Mujahid and al-Rabi' said: it means they do not purify their deeds. Al-Farra' said: Quraysh used to feed the pilgrims, so they forbade that to whoever believed in Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that is never cut off.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: uncut. Muqatil: not diminished, and from it comes "al-Mann," because a person is diminished by it, that is, his strength. Mujahid: not reckoned. It is also said: not reckoned against them. Al-Suddi said: this verse was revealed concerning the sick, the disabled and the aged who are unable to obey; a reward is written for them as the best of what they used to do when they were healthy. [[Fath al-Qadir: 4/506.]]

﴿Say: "Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿And He placed firm mountains upon it, and blessed it﴾, meaning the earth, by what He created in it of benefits. Al-Suddi said: He made its trees grow. ﴿And measured therein its sustenance﴾. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: meaning the provisions of its people and their livelihoods and what sustains them. Mujahid and Qatadah said: He created in it its seas, its rivers, its trees, and its animals, on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ibn Najih related from Mujahid that he said: it is the rain.

Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: He measured in each land within it what He did not place in the other, so that some of them might live from others through trade from land to land. Thus the Sabiri cloth is from Sabur, the tayalisah (shawls) from al-Ray, the ḥabar and the Yemeni cloth from Yemen. This is the narration of Husayn from Mujahid.

Hayyan related from al-Kalbi, who said: bread is for the people of one region, dates for the people of one region, maize for the people of one region, fish for the people of one region, and likewise its counterparts.

﴿In four days﴾: meaning that this together with the first makes four days, as one says: "I married a woman yesterday and two today," and one of them is the one he married yesterday. It is also said: "I came to Wasit in five and to Basra in ten," so the five are part of the ten. Allah the Exalted thus returned the second to the first and summarized it in mention.

﴿Equal﴾: Abu Ja'far put it in the nominative as a beginning, meaning "it is equal." Al-Hasan and Ya'qub put it in the genitive as an attribute of ﴿in four days﴾; the rest put it in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning "they were equalised in equal measure." It is also said it is in the accusative of circumstance and separation. The meaning of the verse: ﴿equal for those who ask﴾ about that. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: for whoever asked about it, so the matter is thus. It is also said: for those who ask Allah for their needs.

Ibn Zayd said: He decreed that in accordance with their questions, for nothing from their questions occurs except that He knew it before it came to be.

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the meaning is "equal for those who ask and those who do not ask," that is, He made clear the matter of the creation of the earth and what is in it to the one who asks and the one who does not, and He gives to the one who asks and the one who does not.

﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾: that is, He set out to create the heaven and aimed at its formation. Istiwa' is among the attributes of acts according to most opinions, and this is indicated by His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven, and it was smoke﴾, vapor of water. ﴿And He said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or by compulsion."﴾ That is, come with what I created in you of benefits, and bring forth, and manifest yourselves with the interests of My creation. Ibn Abbas said: Allah the Exalted said to the heavens: "Rise with your sun, your moon and your stars," and He said to the earth: "Split open your rivers and bring forth your fruits."

﴿They both said: "We come willingly."﴾ He did not say "willingly" in the feminine dual, because He went with it to the heavens and the earth and those within them; its meaning: "We come with those in us, willingly." When He described them by speech, He treated them in the plural as those who understand. It has reached us that one of the prophets said: "O Lord, if the heavens and the earth, when You said to them, 'Come willingly or by compulsion,' had disobeyed You, what would You have done with them?" He said: "I would command one of My creatures, and it would swallow them." He said: "And where is that creature?" He said: "In a meadow of My meadows." He said: "And where is that meadow?" He said: "In the knowledge of My knowledge."

Ibn Abbas recited: ātiyā and ātainā with the long vowel, meaning: "Give obedience from yourselves." They both said: "We have given."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 41, verse 12–20:

﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days,﴾ meaning He perfected them and finished creating them. ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command.﴾ Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this means He created in it its sun, its moon and its stars, and He created in each heaven what He created of angels, and the creation within it, such as the seas and the mountains of hail, and what is not known. It was also said: the meaning is that He revealed to the inhabitants of each heaven the commands and prohibitions that He willed.

﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾, meaning stars. ﴿And as a guard﴾ from the devils who eavesdrop. The word ḥifẓan (as a guard) is in the accusative according to the sense, as if He had said: He made them an adornment and a guard. It was also said: the meaning is "and as a guard We adorned it", with the wāw dropped by assumption, i.e. "and We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps as a guard for it." It was also said: the meaning is "and He guarded it with a guarding."

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning these polytheists, ﴿say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt﴾, meaning I have frightened you, ﴿a punishment like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾, ﴿when the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾, meaning ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the messengers came to them from before them (their predecessors) and from behind them (their successors).

By His saying "from before them" He means the messengers who were sent to their fathers before them, and "from behind them" means those who came after the messengers sent to their fathers, namely the messenger sent to them, Hūd and Ṣāliḥ (peace be upon them). The pronoun in "from before them" refers to ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the pronoun in His saying "from behind them" refers to the messengers.

﴿Saying: Do not worship except Allah.﴾ They said: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾, meaning angels instead of these messengers. ﴿Indeed, we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with.﴾

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid ibn Muḥammad al-Iṣfahānī, who read it to him in Shawwāl of the year 388, who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿUbaydī narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Najdah ibn al-ʿUrayān narrated to us, who said: al-Jammānī narrated to us, who said: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from al-Ajlaḥ, from al-Dhayyāl ibn Ḥarmalah, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The chieftains of Quraysh and Abū Jahl said: The matter of Muhammad has become confused for us. So if you were to seek out a man knowledgeable in poetry, soothsaying and magic, and he went to him, spoke with him, and then came back to us with a clarification of his affair. ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah said: By God, I have heard of poetry, soothsaying and magic, and I have knowledge of that, and it would not be hidden from me if it were so. So he went to him, and when he came out to him, he said: "O Muhammad, are you better than Hāshim? Are you better than ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Are you better than ʿAbd Allāh? Why do you revile our gods and disparage us? If you desire leadership, we will appoint you over our banners, and you will be our chief for as long as you live. If it is women you desire, we will marry you to ten women chosen from whichever houses of Quraysh you wish. If it is wealth you desire, we will gather for you such wealth that you and your descendants after you will be rich." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was silent and did not speak. When he had finished, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are detailed, an Arabic Qur'an…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd.﴾ Then ʿUtbah put his hand over his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship, and he returned to his family and did not go out to Quraysh. Quraysh were held up by ʿUtbah's absence, so Abū Jahl said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by God, we see that ʿUtbah has only turned towards Muhammad and been charmed by his food, and that is only because of some need that has befallen him. Come, let us go to him." So they went to him.

Abū Jahl came to him and said: "By God, O ʿUtbah, what has kept you from us except that you have inclined towards Muhammad and his food has pleased you? If you are in need, we will gather for you from our wealth what will make you independent of Muhammad's food." ʿUtbah became angry and swore that he would never speak to Muhammad again, and said: "By God, you know that I am among the wealthiest of Quraysh, but I went to him, related the account to him, and he answered me with something which, by God, is neither poetry, nor soothsaying, nor magic. ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are detailed…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd.﴾ I put my hand over his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship to desist, and you know that when Muhammad says something, he does not lie, and I feared that punishment would descend upon you."

﴿As for ʿĀd﴾, meaning the people of Hūd, ﴿they waxed arrogant in the land without right and said: Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ That is because they were people of tall bodies and great stature. ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they used to deny Our signs.﴾ ﴿So We sent upon them a violent wind﴾, i.e. a cold, intensely loud and blustering wind. Its root is from ṣarīr (a sound), and it was doubled as one says nahnahtu and kafkaftu. It was also said that the river called Ṣarṣar was named so for the sound of the water flowing in it.

﴿In days of ill omen﴾, consecutive, severe, wretched, and ill-omened for them, in which there was no good at all. Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir and the people of Kufa read nahisāt with a kasra on the ḥāʾ; others read it with a sukūn.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, who said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, who said: Isḥāq ibn Bishr narrated to us, who said: Muqātil narrated to us, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk concerning His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a violent wind﴾, he said: Allah withheld rain from them for three years, and the winds continued upon them without rain. And also from Muqātil, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, and from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: When Allah intends good for a people, He sends rain upon them and withholds from them an abundance of winds; and when Allah intends evil for a people, He withholds rain from them and sends upon them an abundance of winds.

﴿That We may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ ﴿As for Thamūd﴾: al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb read Thamūdu with a ḍamma and tanwīn; and they both did not give it the genitive in the whole Qur'an except His saying ﴿And We gave Thamūd the she-camel﴾ [[Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 59.]], for they did not put it in the genitive here because it is written in the muṣḥaf here without an alif. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿wa-ammā Thamūda﴾ in the accusative without tanwīn, and the rest read it in the nominative without tanwīn.

﴿So We guided them﴾, i.e. We called them and made clear to them. ﴿But they preferred blindness over guidance﴾, i.e. they chose disbelief over faith. ﴿So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them﴾, a destroying [thunderbolt]. Al-hūn means humiliation, and its figurative sense is "one possessing humiliation." ﴿Because of what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.﴾ ﴿And the day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in order﴾, i.e. be brought together and driven, and pushed toward the Fire. Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read nuḥsharu with an open nūn and a damma on the shīn; ʿadāʾa Allāh is in the accusative. Qatādah and al-Suddī said: their first will be held back until their last joins them. ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them about what they used to do.﴾ Al-Suddī and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar said: by "skins" is meant the private parts.

One of the literati recited the verse of ʿĀmir ibn Juwayn:

The man strives for safety, and safety is enough for him,
or he is safe from one whose skin has been wrinkled and whose head has turned white. [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 15/350.]]

And he said: "his skin" is a metaphor for his private part.

So he went to him, and when he came out to him, he said: "O Muhammad, are you better than Hāshim? Are you better than ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Are you better than ʿAbd Allāh? Why do you revile our gods and disparage us? If you desire leadership, we will appoint you over our banners, and you will be our chief for as long as you live. If it is wealth you desire, we will gather for you such wealth that you and your descendants after you will be rich." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was silent and did not speak. When he had finished, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are detailed, an Arabic Qur'an…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd.﴾ Then ʿUtbah put his hand over his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship, and he returned to his family and did not go out to Quraysh. Quraysh were held up by ʿUtbah's absence, so Abū Jahl said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by God, we see that ʿUtbah has only turned towards Muhammad and been charmed by his food, and that is only because of some need that has befallen him. Come, let us go to him." So they went to him.

Abū Jahl came to him and said: "By God, O ʿUtbah, what has kept you from us except that you have inclined towards Muhammad and his food has pleased you? If you are in need, we will gather for you from our wealth what will make you independent of Muhammad's food." ʿUtbah became angry and swore that he would never speak to Muhammad again, and said: "By God, you know that I am among the wealthiest of Quraysh, but I went to him, related the account to him, and he answered me with something which, by God, is neither poetry, nor soothsaying, nor magic. ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are detailed…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd.﴾ I put my hand over his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship to desist, and you know that when Muhammad says something, he does not lie, and I feared that punishment would descend upon you."

And they used to deny Our signs.﴾ ﴿So We sent upon them a violent wind﴾, i.e. a cold, intensely loud and blustering wind. Its root is from ṣarīr (a sound), and it was doubled as one says nahnahtu and kafkaftu. It was also said that the river called Ṣarṣar was named so for the sound of the water flowing in it.

﴿In days of ill omen﴾, consecutive, severe, wretched, and ill-omened for them, in which there was no good at all. Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir and the people of Kufa read nahisāt with a kasra on the ḥāʾ; others read it with a sukūn.

One of the literati recited the verse of ʿĀmir ibn Juwayn:

The man strives for safety, and safety is enough for him,
or he is safe from one whose skin has been wrinkled and whose head has turned white. [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 15/350.]]

And he said: "his skin" is a metaphor for his private part.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 41, verse 12–20:

﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days,﴾ meaning He perfected them and finished creating them. ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command.﴾ Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this means He created in it its sun, its moon and its stars, and He created in each heaven what He created of angels, and the creation within it, such as the seas and the mountains of hail, and what is not known. It was also said: the meaning is that He revealed to the inhabitants of each heaven the commands and prohibitions that He willed.

﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾, meaning stars. ﴿And as a guard﴾ from the devils who eavesdrop. The word ḥifẓan (as a guard) is in the accusative according to the sense, as if He had said: He made them an adornment and a guard. It was also said: the meaning is "and as a guard We adorned it", with the wāw dropped by assumption, i.e. "and We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps as a guard for it." It was also said: the meaning is "and He guarded it with a guarding."

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning these polytheists, ﴿say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt﴾, meaning I have frightened you, ﴿a punishment like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾, ﴿when the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾, meaning ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the messengers came to them from before them (their predecessors) and from behind them (their successors).

﴿Saying: Do not worship except Allah.﴾ They said: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾, meaning angels instead of these messengers. ﴿Indeed, we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with.﴾

Qatādah and al-Suddī said: their first will be held back until their last joins them. ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them about what they used to do.﴾ Al-Suddī and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar said: by "skins" is meant the private parts.

One of the literati recited the verse of ʿĀmir ibn Juwayn:

The man strives for safety, and safety is enough for him,
or he is safe from one whose skin has been wrinkled and whose head has turned white. [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 15/350.]]

And he said: "his skin" is a metaphor for his private part.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 41, verse 12–20:

﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days,﴾ meaning He perfected them and finished creating them. ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command.﴾ Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this means He created in it its sun, its moon and its stars, and He created in each heaven what He created of angels, and the creation within it, such as the seas and the mountains of hail, and what is not known. It was also said: the meaning is that He revealed to the inhabitants of each heaven the commands and prohibitions that He willed.

﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾, meaning stars. ﴿And as a guard﴾ from the devils who eavesdrop. The word ḥifẓan (as a guard) is in the accusative according to the sense, as if He had said: He made them an adornment and a guard. It was also said: the meaning is "and as a guard We adorned it", with the wāw dropped by assumption, i.e. "and We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps as a guard for it." It was also said: the meaning is "and He guarded it with a guarding."

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning these polytheists, ﴿say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt﴾, meaning I have frightened you, ﴿a punishment like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾, ﴿when the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾, meaning ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the messengers came to them from before them (their predecessors) and from behind them (their successors).

By His saying "from before them" He means the messengers who were sent to their fathers before them, and "from behind them" means those who came after the messengers sent to their fathers, namely the messenger sent to them, Hūd and Ṣāliḥ (peace be upon them). The pronoun in "from before them" refers to ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the pronoun in His saying "from behind them" refers to the messengers.

﴿Saying: Do not worship except Allah.﴾ They said: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾, meaning angels instead of these messengers. ﴿Indeed, we are disbelievers in what you have been sent with.﴾

We were informed by Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid ibn Muḥammad al-Iṣfahānī, who read it to him in Shawwāl of the year 388, who said: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿUbaydī narrated to us, who said: Aḥmad ibn Najdah ibn al-ʿUrayān narrated to us, who said: al-Jammānī narrated to us, who said: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from al-Ajlaḥ, from al-Dhayyāl ibn Ḥarmalah, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: The chieftains of Quraysh and Abū Jahl said: The matter of Muhammad has become confused for us. So if you were to seek out a man knowledgeable in poetry, soothsaying and magic, and he went to him, spoke with him, and then came back to us with a clarification of his affair. ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah said: By God, I have heard of poetry, soothsaying and magic, and I have knowledge of that, and it would not be hidden from me if it were so. So he went to him, and when he came out to him, he said: "O Muhammad, are you better than Hāshim? Are you better than ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib? Are you better than ʿAbd Allāh? Why do you revile our gods and disparage us? If you desire leadership, we will appoint you over our banners, and you will be our chief for as long as you live. If it is women you desire, we will marry you to ten women chosen from whichever houses of Quraysh you wish. If it is wealth you desire, we will gather for you such wealth that you and your descendants after you will be rich." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was silent and did not speak. When he had finished, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are detailed, an Arabic Qur'an…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd.﴾ Then ʿUtbah put his hand over his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship, and he returned to his family and did not go out to Quraysh. Quraysh were held up by ʿUtbah's absence, so Abū Jahl said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by God, we see that ʿUtbah has only turned towards Muhammad and been charmed by his food, and that is only because of some need that has befallen him. Come, let us go to him." So they went to him.

Abū Jahl came to him and said: "By God, O ʿUtbah, what has kept you from us except that you have inclined towards Muhammad and his food has pleased you? If you are in need, we will gather for you from our wealth what will make you independent of Muhammad's food." ʿUtbah became angry and swore that he would never speak to Muhammad again, and said: "By God, you know that I am among the wealthiest of Quraysh, but I went to him, related the account to him, and he answered me with something which, by God, is neither poetry, nor soothsaying, nor magic. ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ḥā Mīm. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses are detailed…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd.﴾ I put my hand over his mouth and implored him by the ties of kinship to desist, and you know that when Muhammad says something, he does not lie, and I feared that punishment would descend upon you."

﴿As for ʿĀd﴾, meaning the people of Hūd, ﴿they waxed arrogant in the land without right and said: Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ That is because they were people of tall bodies and great stature. ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they used to deny Our signs.﴾ ﴿So We sent upon them a violent wind﴾, i.e. a cold, intensely loud and blustering wind. Its root is from ṣarīr (a sound), and it was doubled as one says nahnahtu and kafkaftu. It was also said that the river called Ṣarṣar was named so for the sound of the water flowing in it.

﴿In days of ill omen﴾, consecutive, severe, wretched, and ill-omened for them, in which there was no good at all. Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir and the people of Kufa read nahisāt with a kasra on the ḥāʾ; others read it with a sukūn.

We were informed by Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Mukhallad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, who said: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, who said: Isḥāq ibn Bishr narrated to us, who said: Muqātil narrated to us, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk concerning His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them a violent wind﴾, he said: Allah withheld rain from them for three years, and the winds continued upon them without rain. And also from Muqātil, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, and from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: When Allah intends good for a people, He sends rain upon them and withholds from them an abundance of winds; and when Allah intends evil for a people, He withholds rain from them and sends upon them an abundance of winds.

﴿That We may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.﴾ ﴿As for Thamūd﴾: al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Wathhāb read Thamūdu with a ḍamma and tanwīn; and they both did not give it the genitive in the whole Qur'an except His saying ﴿And We gave Thamūd the she-camel﴾ [[Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 59.]], for they did not put it in the genitive here because it is written in the muṣḥaf here without an alif. Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿wa-ammā Thamūda﴾ in the accusative without tanwīn, and the rest read it in the nominative without tanwīn.

﴿So We guided them﴾, i.e. We called them and made clear to them. ﴿But they preferred blindness over guidance﴾, i.e. they chose disbelief over faith. ﴿So the thunderbolt of the humiliating punishment seized them﴾, a destroying [thunderbolt]. Al-hūn means humiliation, and its figurative sense is "one possessing humiliation." ﴿Because of what they used to earn.﴾ ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah.﴾ ﴿And the day when the enemies of Allah will be gathered to the Fire, they will be driven in order﴾, i.e. be brought together and driven, and pushed toward the Fire. Nāfiʿ and Yaʿqūb read nuḥsharu with an open nūn and a damma on the shīn; ʿadāʾa Allāh is in the accusative. Qatādah and al-Suddī said: their first will be held back until their last joins them. ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their eyes and their skins will testify against them about what they used to do.﴾ Al-Suddī and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar said: by "skins" is meant the private parts.

One of the literati recited the verse of ʿĀmir ibn Juwayn:

The man strives for safety, and safety is enough for him,
or he is safe from one whose skin has been wrinkled and whose head has turned white. [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 15/350.]]

And he said: "his skin" is a metaphor for his private part.

And they say, meaning the disbelievers who are gathered to the Fire: ﴿To their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, Shurayk informed us, from Ubayd al-Makit, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day until his molars showed, then said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?"

They said: "What did you laugh at, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I was amazed at the servant's dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says, 'O Lord, did You not promise that You would not wrong me?' He says, 'Indeed.' He says, 'Then I accept no witness against myself except my own self.' He says, 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do."

He said: "Then he will say to them, 'Away with you! Perish! It was on your behalf that I was disputing.'" [161] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 7/55.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ That is, "you were not concealing yourselves" means you were hiding yourselves, according to the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "you were fearing (taqun)." Qatada said: "you were thinking."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Warraq related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir and Abu Hudhayfa related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men came: a man from Thaqif and two sons-in-law from Quraysh. Their bellies were full of fat, and their understanding was little. They spoke among themselves, and one of them said, 'Do you think He hears what we say?' The other said, 'If we raise our voices He hears, and if we lower them He does not hear.' Another said, 'If He hears when we raise our voices, then He hears when we lower them.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him of that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...you became among the losers.﴾"

The Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two sons-in-law from Quraysh were Rabi'a and Safwan ibn Umayya.

﴿And that was your thinking, which you thought of your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ "Destroyed you" means caused you to perish. Qatada said: "Here, 'thinking' means knowledge."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, for a people who thought ill of their Lord were destroyed by it." That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And that was your thinking...﴾ the verse. [162] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/353.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us, Ahmad ibn Hafs related to us, my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am according to My servant's thought of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me." [163] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/412.]]

Qatada said: "Whoever among you is able to die while thinking well of his Lord, let him do so, for thinking is of two kinds: a thought that saves, and a thought that destroys." Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Bahili said:

"The one who thinks well is at rest;
the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Mansur related to us, Miskin Abu Fatima related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience." Mujahid and Ikrima said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Him." Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: "They remained steadfast in the worship and obedience of Allah." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not deviate." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They acted in accordance with what they said." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They remained steadfast upon knowledge and did not apostatize." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "They remained steadfast upon the fact that Allah is their Lord." Al-Rabi' said: "They turned away from all besides Allah the Exalted." Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "They renounced the perishable and desired the enduring." Some of them said: "They remained steadfast in secret as they remained steadfast in declaration." It was also said: "They remained steadfast in deed as they remained steadfast in word."

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "My community, and by the Lord of the Ka'ba." [164] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/358.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sunni related to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn Hayyan al-Jumahi related to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a matter to hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then remain steadfast." I said: "What is the thing you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own tongue and said: "This." [165] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/413.]]

It is also narrated that a delegation came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to them, then wept. They said: "Do you weep out of fear of the One who sent you?" He said: "Yes. I have been sent upon a path like the edge of a sword: if I remain steadfast I am saved, and if I swerve from it I am destroyed." [166] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/201, with variation.]]

Qatada said: "When al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

﴿The angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve."﴾ Qatada said: "When they rise from their graves." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah al-Basri said: "It occurs in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, that they should not fear nor grieve." Abu al-Aliya said: "Do not fear regarding what you have done, and do not grieve over what you have left behind." Mujahid said: "Do not fear what you are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind in your worldly life of family, children, and offspring, for We shall replace you in all of that." Al-Suddi said: "Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you." Ata ibn Rabah said: "Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them for you."

The people of language said regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ with fidelity to abandoning harshness, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ with contentment, ﴿saying: Do not fear﴾ hardship, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over perishing, ﴿and rejoice in the Garden with which you were promised﴾ in meeting. "Do not fear," for there is no fear upon the people of steadfastness; "do not grieve," for you have all kinds of honour; "and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of safety." Do not fear, for you have held fast to the religion of Allah; do not grieve, for you have held fast to the rope of Allah; and rejoice in the Garden, even if you were doubtful and grieved. Do not grieve, for you have long been fearful; do not grieve, for you have attained what you sought; and rejoice in the Garden, in which you desired. Do not fear, for you are the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are the people of forgiveness; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of good pleasure. Do not fear, for you are the people of martyrdom; do not grieve, for you are the people of felicity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of increase. Do not fear, for you are the people of gifts; do not grieve, for you are the people of union; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of majesty. Do not fear, for you are safe from destruction; do not grieve, for the time of joy has come to you; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of delight. Do not fear, for your effort is appreciated; do not grieve, for your sin is forgiven; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of... Do not fear, for you have long been among the fearful; do not grieve, for you have been among the knowers; and rejoice in the Garden, which the describers cannot describe. Do not fear, for there is no fear upon the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are not among the deprived; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of faith. Do not fear, for you are not among the people of Hellfire; do not grieve, for you have reached the Lord, the Merciful; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of bliss. Do not fear, for fear has been removed from you; do not grieve, for you have been saved from every calamity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of hospitality. Do not grieve over removal from authority; do not grieve over what you have previously done of betrayal; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of guidance. Do not fear the descent of punishment; do not grieve over the terror of the reckoning; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of reward. Do not fear, for you are safe from punishment; do not grieve, for you will reach reward; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is an excellent return. Do not fear, for you are the people of fidelity; do not grieve over what you have earned of harshness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of purity. Do not fear, for you are safe from ruin; do not grieve, for you have been saved from weariness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of delight.

﴿We are your allies﴾

The angels who descend upon them with glad tidings say: ﴿We are your allies﴾, your helpers and your friends, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We are your allies﴾ means: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world," and ﴿We are your allies...in the Hereafter.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ibn Khalid informed us, Dawud ibn Amr al-Dabbi informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "They are their companions who were with them in the world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will say: 'We will not leave you until we bring you into the Garden.'"

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾, that is, what you wish, request, and wish for. The original phrase is: whatever you claim is yours, it is yours by the judgment of your Lord.

﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾: that is, this was made as provision. ﴿From One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And they say, meaning the disbelievers who are gathered to the Fire: ﴿To their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, Shurayk informed us, from Ubayd al-Makit, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day until his molars showed, then said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?"

They said: "What did you laugh at, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I was amazed at the servant's dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says, 'O Lord, did You not promise that You would not wrong me?' He says, 'Indeed.' He says, 'Then I accept no witness against myself except my own self.' He says, 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do."

He said: "Then he will say to them, 'Away with you! Perish! It was on your behalf that I was disputing.'" [161] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 7/55.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ That is, "you were not concealing yourselves" means you were hiding yourselves, according to the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "you were fearing (taqun)." Qatada said: "you were thinking."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Warraq related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir and Abu Hudhayfa related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men came: a man from Thaqif and two sons-in-law from Quraysh. Their bellies were full of fat, and their understanding was little. They spoke among themselves, and one of them said, 'Do you think He hears what we say?' The other said, 'If we raise our voices He hears, and if we lower them He does not hear.' Another said, 'If He hears when we raise our voices, then He hears when we lower them.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him of that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...you became among the losers.﴾"

The Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two sons-in-law from Quraysh were Rabi'a and Safwan ibn Umayya.

﴿And that was your thinking, which you thought of your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ "Destroyed you" means caused you to perish. Qatada said: "Here, 'thinking' means knowledge."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, for a people who thought ill of their Lord were destroyed by it." That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And that was your thinking...﴾ the verse. [162] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/353.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us, Ahmad ibn Hafs related to us, my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am according to My servant's thought of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me." [163] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/412.]]

Qatada said: "Whoever among you is able to die while thinking well of his Lord, let him do so, for thinking is of two kinds: a thought that saves, and a thought that destroys." Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Bahili said:

"The one who thinks well is at rest;
the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Mansur related to us, Miskin Abu Fatima related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience." Mujahid and Ikrima said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Him." Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: "They remained steadfast in the worship and obedience of Allah." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not deviate." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They acted in accordance with what they said." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They remained steadfast upon knowledge and did not apostatize." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "They remained steadfast upon the fact that Allah is their Lord." Al-Rabi' said: "They turned away from all besides Allah the Exalted." Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "They renounced the perishable and desired the enduring." Some of them said: "They remained steadfast in secret as they remained steadfast in declaration." It was also said: "They remained steadfast in deed as they remained steadfast in word."

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "My community, and by the Lord of the Ka'ba." [164] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/358.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sunni related to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn Hayyan al-Jumahi related to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a matter to hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then remain steadfast." I said: "What is the thing you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own tongue and said: "This." [165] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/413.]]

It is also narrated that a delegation came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to them, then wept. They said: "Do you weep out of fear of the One who sent you?" He said: "Yes. I have been sent upon a path like the edge of a sword: if I remain steadfast I am saved, and if I swerve from it I am destroyed." [166] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/201, with variation.]]

Qatada said: "When al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

﴿The angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve."﴾ Qatada said: "When they rise from their graves." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah al-Basri said: "It occurs in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, that they should not fear nor grieve." Abu al-Aliya said: "Do not fear regarding what you have done, and do not grieve over what you have left behind." Mujahid said: "Do not fear what you are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind in your worldly life of family, children, and offspring, for We shall replace you in all of that." Al-Suddi said: "Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you." Ata ibn Rabah said: "Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them for you."

The people of language said regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ with fidelity to abandoning harshness, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ with contentment, ﴿saying: Do not fear﴾ hardship, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over perishing, ﴿and rejoice in the Garden with which you were promised﴾ in meeting. "Do not fear," for there is no fear upon the people of steadfastness; "do not grieve," for you have all kinds of honour; "and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of safety." Do not fear, for you have held fast to the religion of Allah; do not grieve, for you have held fast to the rope of Allah; and rejoice in the Garden, even if you were doubtful and grieved. Do not grieve, for you have long been fearful; do not grieve, for you have attained what you sought; and rejoice in the Garden, in which you desired. Do not fear, for you are the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are the people of forgiveness; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of good pleasure. Do not fear, for you are the people of martyrdom; do not grieve, for you are the people of felicity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of increase. Do not fear, for you are the people of gifts; do not grieve, for you are the people of union; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of majesty. Do not fear, for you are safe from destruction; do not grieve, for the time of joy has come to you; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of delight. Do not fear, for your effort is appreciated; do not grieve, for your sin is forgiven; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of... Do not fear, for you have long been among the fearful; do not grieve, for you have been among the knowers; and rejoice in the Garden, which the describers cannot describe. Do not fear, for there is no fear upon the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are not among the deprived; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of faith. Do not fear, for you are not among the people of Hellfire; do not grieve, for you have reached the Lord, the Merciful; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of bliss. Do not fear, for fear has been removed from you; do not grieve, for you have been saved from every calamity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of hospitality. Do not grieve over removal from authority; do not grieve over what you have previously done of betrayal; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of guidance. Do not fear the descent of punishment; do not grieve over the terror of the reckoning; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of reward. Do not fear, for you are safe from punishment; do not grieve, for you will reach reward; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is an excellent return. Do not fear, for you are the people of fidelity; do not grieve over what you have earned of harshness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of purity. Do not fear, for you are safe from ruin; do not grieve, for you have been saved from weariness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of delight.

﴿We are your allies﴾

The angels who descend upon them with glad tidings say: ﴿We are your allies﴾, your helpers and your friends, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We are your allies﴾ means: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world," and ﴿We are your allies...in the Hereafter.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ibn Khalid informed us, Dawud ibn Amr al-Dabbi informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "They are their companions who were with them in the world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will say: 'We will not leave you until we bring you into the Garden.'"

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾, that is, what you wish, request, and wish for. The original phrase is: whatever you claim is yours, it is yours by the judgment of your Lord.

﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾: that is, this was made as provision. ﴿From One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And they say, meaning the disbelievers who are gathered to the Fire: ﴿To their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, Shurayk informed us, from Ubayd al-Makit, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day until his molars showed, then said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?"

They said: "What did you laugh at, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I was amazed at the servant's dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says, 'O Lord, did You not promise that You would not wrong me?' He says, 'Indeed.' He says, 'Then I accept no witness against myself except my own self.' He says, 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do."

He said: "Then he will say to them, 'Away with you! Perish! It was on your behalf that I was disputing.'" [161] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 7/55.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ That is, "you were not concealing yourselves" means you were hiding yourselves, according to the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "you were fearing (taqun)." Qatada said: "you were thinking."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Warraq related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir and Abu Hudhayfa related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men came: a man from Thaqif and two sons-in-law from Quraysh. Their bellies were full of fat, and their understanding was little. They spoke among themselves, and one of them said, 'Do you think He hears what we say?' The other said, 'If we raise our voices He hears, and if we lower them He does not hear.' Another said, 'If He hears when we raise our voices, then He hears when we lower them.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him of that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...you became among the losers.﴾"

The Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two sons-in-law from Quraysh were Rabi'a and Safwan ibn Umayya.

﴿And that was your thinking, which you thought of your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ "Destroyed you" means caused you to perish. Qatada said: "Here, 'thinking' means knowledge."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, for a people who thought ill of their Lord were destroyed by it." That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And that was your thinking...﴾ the verse. [162] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/353.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us, Ahmad ibn Hafs related to us, my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am according to My servant's thought of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me." [163] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/412.]]

Qatada said: "Whoever among you is able to die while thinking well of his Lord, let him do so, for thinking is of two kinds: a thought that saves, and a thought that destroys." Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Bahili said:

"The one who thinks well is at rest;
the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."
