the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Mansur related to us, Miskin Abu Fatima related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience." Mujahid and Ikrima said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Him." Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: "They remained steadfast in the worship and obedience of Allah." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not deviate." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They acted in accordance with what they said." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They remained steadfast upon knowledge and did not apostatize." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "They remained steadfast upon the fact that Allah is their Lord." Al-Rabi' said: "They turned away from all besides Allah the Exalted." Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "They renounced the perishable and desired the enduring." Some of them said: "They remained steadfast in secret as they remained steadfast in declaration." It was also said: "They remained steadfast in deed as they remained steadfast in word."

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "My community, and by the Lord of the Ka'ba." [164] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/358.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sunni related to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn Hayyan al-Jumahi related to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a matter to hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then remain steadfast." I said: "What is the thing you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own tongue and said: "This." [165] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/413.]]

It is also narrated that a delegation came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to them, then wept. They said: "Do you weep out of fear of the One who sent you?" He said: "Yes. I have been sent upon a path like the edge of a sword: if I remain steadfast I am saved, and if I swerve from it I am destroyed." [166] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/201, with variation.]]

Qatada said: "When al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

﴿The angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve."﴾ Qatada said: "When they rise from their graves." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah al-Basri said: "It occurs in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, that they should not fear nor grieve." Abu al-Aliya said: "Do not fear regarding what you have done, and do not grieve over what you have left behind." Mujahid said: "Do not fear what you are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind in your worldly life of family, children, and offspring, for We shall replace you in all of that." Al-Suddi said: "Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you." Ata ibn Rabah said: "Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them for you."

The people of language said regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ with fidelity to abandoning harshness, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ with contentment, ﴿saying: Do not fear﴾ hardship, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over perishing, ﴿and rejoice in the Garden with which you were promised﴾ in meeting. "Do not fear," for there is no fear upon the people of steadfastness; "do not grieve," for you have all kinds of honour; "and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of safety." Do not fear, for you have held fast to the religion of Allah; do not grieve, for you have held fast to the rope of Allah; and rejoice in the Garden, even if you were doubtful and grieved. Do not grieve, for you have long been fearful; do not grieve, for you have attained what you sought; and rejoice in the Garden, in which you desired. Do not fear, for you are the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are the people of forgiveness; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of good pleasure. Do not fear, for you are the people of martyrdom; do not grieve, for you are the people of felicity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of increase. Do not fear, for you are the people of gifts; do not grieve, for you are the people of union; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of majesty. Do not fear, for you are safe from destruction; do not grieve, for the time of joy has come to you; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of delight. Do not fear, for your effort is appreciated; do not grieve, for your sin is forgiven; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of... Do not fear, for you have long been among the fearful; do not grieve, for you have been among the knowers; and rejoice in the Garden, which the describers cannot describe. Do not fear, for there is no fear upon the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are not among the deprived; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of faith. Do not fear, for you are not among the people of Hellfire; do not grieve, for you have reached the Lord, the Merciful; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of bliss. Do not fear, for fear has been removed from you; do not grieve, for you have been saved from every calamity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of hospitality. Do not grieve over removal from authority; do not grieve over what you have previously done of betrayal; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of guidance. Do not fear the descent of punishment; do not grieve over the terror of the reckoning; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of reward. Do not fear, for you are safe from punishment; do not grieve, for you will reach reward; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is an excellent return. Do not fear, for you are the people of fidelity; do not grieve over what you have earned of harshness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of purity. Do not fear, for you are safe from ruin; do not grieve, for you have been saved from weariness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of delight.

﴿We are your allies﴾

The angels who descend upon them with glad tidings say: ﴿We are your allies﴾, your helpers and your friends, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We are your allies﴾ means: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world," and ﴿We are your allies...in the Hereafter.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ibn Khalid informed us, Dawud ibn Amr al-Dabbi informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "They are their companions who were with them in the world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will say: 'We will not leave you until we bring you into the Garden.'"

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾, that is, what you wish, request, and wish for. The original phrase is: whatever you claim is yours, it is yours by the judgment of your Lord.

﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾: that is, this was made as provision. ﴿From One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And they say, meaning the disbelievers who are gathered to the Fire: ﴿To their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, Shurayk informed us, from Ubayd al-Makit, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day until his molars showed, then said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?"

They said: "What did you laugh at, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I was amazed at the servant's dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says, 'O Lord, did You not promise that You would not wrong me?' He says, 'Indeed.' He says, 'Then I accept no witness against myself except my own self.' He says, 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do."

He said: "Then he will say to them, 'Away with you! Perish! It was on your behalf that I was disputing.'" [161] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 7/55.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ That is, "you were not concealing yourselves" means you were hiding yourselves, according to the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "you were fearing (taqun)." Qatada said: "you were thinking."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Warraq related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir and Abu Hudhayfa related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men came: a man from Thaqif and two sons-in-law from Quraysh. Their bellies were full of fat, and their understanding was little. They spoke among themselves, and one of them said, 'Do you think He hears what we say?' The other said, 'If we raise our voices He hears, and if we lower them He does not hear.' Another said, 'If He hears when we raise our voices, then He hears when we lower them.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him of that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...you became among the losers.﴾"

The Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two sons-in-law from Quraysh were Rabi'a and Safwan ibn Umayya.

﴿And that was your thinking, which you thought of your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ "Destroyed you" means caused you to perish. Qatada said: "Here, 'thinking' means knowledge."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, for a people who thought ill of their Lord were destroyed by it." That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And that was your thinking...﴾ the verse. [162] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/353.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us, Ahmad ibn Hafs related to us, my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am according to My servant's thought of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me." [163] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/412.]]

Qatada said: "Whoever among you is able to die while thinking well of his Lord, let him do so, for thinking is of two kinds: a thought that saves, and a thought that destroys." Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Bahili said:

"The one who thinks well is at rest;
the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Mansur related to us, Miskin Abu Fatima related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience." Mujahid and Ikrima said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Him." Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: "They remained steadfast in the worship and obedience of Allah." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not deviate." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They acted in accordance with what they said." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They remained steadfast upon knowledge and did not apostatize." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "They remained steadfast upon the fact that Allah is their Lord." Al-Rabi' said: "They turned away from all besides Allah the Exalted." Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "They renounced the perishable and desired the enduring." Some of them said: "They remained steadfast in secret as they remained steadfast in declaration." It was also said: "They remained steadfast in deed as they remained steadfast in word."

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "My community, and by the Lord of the Ka'ba." [164] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/358.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sunni related to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn Hayyan al-Jumahi related to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a matter to hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then remain steadfast." I said: "What is the thing you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own tongue and said: "This." [165] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/413.]]

It is also narrated that a delegation came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to them, then wept. They said: "Do you weep out of fear of the One who sent you?" He said: "Yes. I have been sent upon a path like the edge of a sword: if I remain steadfast I am saved, and if I swerve from it I am destroyed." [166] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/201, with variation.]]

Qatada said: "When al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

﴿The angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve."﴾ Qatada said: "When they rise from their graves." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah al-Basri said: "It occurs in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, that they should not fear nor grieve." Abu al-Aliya said: "Do not fear regarding what you have done, and do not grieve over what you have left behind." Mujahid said: "Do not fear what you are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind in your worldly life of family, children, and offspring, for We shall replace you in all of that." Al-Suddi said: "Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you." Ata ibn Rabah said: "Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them for you."

The people of language said regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ with fidelity to abandoning harshness, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ with contentment, ﴿saying: Do not fear﴾ hardship, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over perishing, ﴿and rejoice in the Garden with which you were promised﴾ in meeting. "Do not fear," for there is no fear upon the people of steadfastness; "do not grieve," for you have all kinds of honour; "and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of safety." Do not fear, for you have held fast to the religion of Allah; do not grieve, for you have held fast to the rope of Allah; and rejoice in the Garden, even if you were doubtful and grieved. Do not grieve, for you have long been fearful; do not grieve, for you have attained what you sought; and rejoice in the Garden, in which you desired. Do not fear, for you are the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are the people of forgiveness; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of good pleasure. Do not fear, for you are the people of martyrdom; do not grieve, for you are the people of felicity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of increase. Do not fear, for you are the people of gifts; do not grieve, for you are the people of union; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of majesty. Do not fear, for you are safe from destruction; do not grieve, for the time of joy has come to you; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of delight. Do not fear, for your effort is appreciated; do not grieve, for your sin is forgiven; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of... Do not fear, for you have long been among the fearful; do not grieve, for you have been among the knowers; and rejoice in the Garden, which the describers cannot describe. Do not fear, for there is no fear upon the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are not among the deprived; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of faith. Do not fear, for you are not among the people of Hellfire; do not grieve, for you have reached the Lord, the Merciful; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of bliss. Do not fear, for fear has been removed from you; do not grieve, for you have been saved from every calamity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of hospitality. Do not grieve over removal from authority; do not grieve over what you have previously done of betrayal; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of guidance. Do not fear the descent of punishment; do not grieve over the terror of the reckoning; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of reward. Do not fear, for you are safe from punishment; do not grieve, for you will reach reward; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is an excellent return. Do not fear, for you are the people of fidelity; do not grieve over what you have earned of harshness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of purity. Do not fear, for you are safe from ruin; do not grieve, for you have been saved from weariness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of delight.

﴿We are your allies﴾

The angels who descend upon them with glad tidings say: ﴿We are your allies﴾, your helpers and your friends, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We are your allies﴾ means: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world," and ﴿We are your allies...in the Hereafter.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ibn Khalid informed us, Dawud ibn Amr al-Dabbi informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "They are their companions who were with them in the world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will say: 'We will not leave you until we bring you into the Garden.'"

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾, that is, what you wish, request, and wish for. The original phrase is: whatever you claim is yours, it is yours by the judgment of your Lord.

﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾: that is, this was made as provision. ﴿From One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And they say, meaning the disbelievers who are gathered to the Fire: ﴿To their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, Shurayk informed us, from Ubayd al-Makit, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day until his molars showed, then said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?"

They said: "What did you laugh at, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I was amazed at the servant's dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says, 'O Lord, did You not promise that You would not wrong me?' He says, 'Indeed.' He says, 'Then I accept no witness against myself except my own self.' He says, 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do."

He said: "Then he will say to them, 'Away with you! Perish! It was on your behalf that I was disputing.'" [161] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 7/55.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ That is, "you were not concealing yourselves" means you were hiding yourselves, according to the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "you were fearing (taqun)." Qatada said: "you were thinking."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Warraq related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir and Abu Hudhayfa related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men came: a man from Thaqif and two sons-in-law from Quraysh. Their bellies were full of fat, and their understanding was little. They spoke among themselves, and one of them said, 'Do you think He hears what we say?' The other said, 'If we raise our voices He hears, and if we lower them He does not hear.' Another said, 'If He hears when we raise our voices, then He hears when we lower them.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him of that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...you became among the losers.﴾"

The Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two sons-in-law from Quraysh were Rabi'a and Safwan ibn Umayya.

﴿And that was your thinking, which you thought of your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ "Destroyed you" means caused you to perish. Qatada said: "Here, 'thinking' means knowledge."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, for a people who thought ill of their Lord were destroyed by it." That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And that was your thinking...﴾ the verse. [162] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/353.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us, Ahmad ibn Hafs related to us, my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am according to My servant's thought of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me." [163] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/412.]]

Qatada said: "Whoever among you is able to die while thinking well of his Lord, let him do so, for thinking is of two kinds: a thought that saves, and a thought that destroys." Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Bahili said:

"The one who thinks well is at rest;
the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Mansur related to us, Miskin Abu Fatima related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience." Mujahid and Ikrima said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Him." Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: "They remained steadfast in the worship and obedience of Allah." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not deviate." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They acted in accordance with what they said." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They remained steadfast upon knowledge and did not apostatize." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "They remained steadfast upon the fact that Allah is their Lord." Al-Rabi' said: "They turned away from all besides Allah the Exalted." Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "They renounced the perishable and desired the enduring." Some of them said: "They remained steadfast in secret as they remained steadfast in declaration." It was also said: "They remained steadfast in deed as they remained steadfast in word."

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "My community, and by the Lord of the Ka'ba." [164] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/358.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sunni related to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn Hayyan al-Jumahi related to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a matter to hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then remain steadfast." I said: "What is the thing you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own tongue and said: "This." [165] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/413.]]

It is also narrated that a delegation came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to them, then wept. They said: "Do you weep out of fear of the One who sent you?" He said: "Yes. I have been sent upon a path like the edge of a sword: if I remain steadfast I am saved, and if I swerve from it I am destroyed." [166] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/201, with variation.]]

Qatada said: "When al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

﴿The angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve."﴾ Qatada said: "When they rise from their graves." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah al-Basri said: "It occurs in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, that they should not fear nor grieve." Abu al-Aliya said: "Do not fear regarding what you have done, and do not grieve over what you have left behind." Mujahid said: "Do not fear what you are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind in your worldly life of family, children, and offspring, for We shall replace you in all of that." Al-Suddi said: "Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you." Ata ibn Rabah said: "Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them for you."

The people of language said regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ with fidelity to abandoning harshness, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ with contentment, ﴿saying: Do not fear﴾ hardship, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over perishing, ﴿and rejoice in the Garden with which you were promised﴾ in meeting. "Do not fear," for there is no fear upon the people of steadfastness; "do not grieve," for you have all kinds of honour; "and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of safety." Do not fear, for you have held fast to the religion of Allah; do not grieve, for you have held fast to the rope of Allah; and rejoice in the Garden, even if you were doubtful and grieved. Do not grieve, for you have long been fearful; do not grieve, for you have attained what you sought; and rejoice in the Garden, in which you desired. Do not fear, for you are the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are the people of forgiveness; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of good pleasure. Do not fear, for you are the people of martyrdom; do not grieve, for you are the people of felicity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of increase. Do not fear, for you are the people of gifts; do not grieve, for you are the people of union; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of majesty. Do not fear, for you are safe from destruction; do not grieve, for the time of joy has come to you; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of delight. Do not fear, for your effort is appreciated; do not grieve, for your sin is forgiven; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of... Do not fear, for you have long been among the fearful; do not grieve, for you have been among the knowers; and rejoice in the Garden, which the describers cannot describe. Do not fear, for there is no fear upon the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are not among the deprived; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of faith. Do not fear, for you are not among the people of Hellfire; do not grieve, for you have reached the Lord, the Merciful; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of bliss. Do not fear, for fear has been removed from you; do not grieve, for you have been saved from every calamity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of hospitality. Do not grieve over removal from authority; do not grieve over what you have previously done of betrayal; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of guidance. Do not fear the descent of punishment; do not grieve over the terror of the reckoning; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of reward. Do not fear, for you are safe from punishment; do not grieve, for you will reach reward; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is an excellent return. Do not fear, for you are the people of fidelity; do not grieve over what you have earned of harshness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of purity. Do not fear, for you are safe from ruin; do not grieve, for you have been saved from weariness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of delight.

﴿We are your allies﴾

The angels who descend upon them with glad tidings say: ﴿We are your allies﴾, your helpers and your friends, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We are your allies﴾ means: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world," and ﴿We are your allies...in the Hereafter.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ibn Khalid informed us, Dawud ibn Amr al-Dabbi informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "They are their companions who were with them in the world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will say: 'We will not leave you until we bring you into the Garden.'"

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾, that is, what you wish, request, and wish for. The original phrase is: whatever you claim is yours, it is yours by the judgment of your Lord.

﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾: that is, this was made as provision. ﴿From One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And they say, meaning the disbelievers who are gathered to the Fire: ﴿To their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, Shurayk informed us, from Ubayd al-Makit, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day until his molars showed, then said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?"

They said: "What did you laugh at, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I was amazed at the servant's dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says, 'O Lord, did You not promise that You would not wrong me?' He says, 'Indeed.' He says, 'Then I accept no witness against myself except my own self.' He says, 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do."

He said: "Then he will say to them, 'Away with you! Perish! It was on your behalf that I was disputing.'" [161] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 7/55.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ That is, "you were not concealing yourselves" means you were hiding yourselves, according to the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "you were fearing (taqun)." Qatada said: "you were thinking."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Warraq related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir and Abu Hudhayfa related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men came: a man from Thaqif and two sons-in-law from Quraysh. Their bellies were full of fat, and their understanding was little. They spoke among themselves, and one of them said, 'Do you think He hears what we say?' The other said, 'If we raise our voices He hears, and if we lower them He does not hear.' Another said, 'If He hears when we raise our voices, then He hears when we lower them.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him of that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...you became among the losers.﴾"

The Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two sons-in-law from Quraysh were Rabi'a and Safwan ibn Umayya.

﴿And that was your thinking, which you thought of your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ "Destroyed you" means caused you to perish. Qatada said: "Here, 'thinking' means knowledge."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, for a people who thought ill of their Lord were destroyed by it." That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And that was your thinking...﴾ the verse. [162] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/353.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us, Ahmad ibn Hafs related to us, my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am according to My servant's thought of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me." [163] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/412.]]

Qatada said: "Whoever among you is able to die while thinking well of his Lord, let him do so, for thinking is of two kinds: a thought that saves, and a thought that destroys." Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Bahili said:

"The one who thinks well is at rest;
the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Mansur related to us, Miskin Abu Fatima related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience." Mujahid and Ikrima said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Him." Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: "They remained steadfast in the worship and obedience of Allah." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not deviate." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They acted in accordance with what they said." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They remained steadfast upon knowledge and did not apostatize." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "They remained steadfast upon the fact that Allah is their Lord." Al-Rabi' said: "They turned away from all besides Allah the Exalted." Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "They renounced the perishable and desired the enduring." Some of them said: "They remained steadfast in secret as they remained steadfast in declaration." It was also said: "They remained steadfast in deed as they remained steadfast in word."

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "My community, and by the Lord of the Ka'ba." [164] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/358.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sunni related to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn Hayyan al-Jumahi related to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a matter to hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then remain steadfast." I said: "What is the thing you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own tongue and said: "This." [165] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/413.]]

It is also narrated that a delegation came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to them, then wept. They said: "Do you weep out of fear of the One who sent you?" He said: "Yes. I have been sent upon a path like the edge of a sword: if I remain steadfast I am saved, and if I swerve from it I am destroyed." [166] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/201, with variation.]]

Qatada said: "When al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

﴿The angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve."﴾ Qatada said: "When they rise from their graves." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah al-Basri said: "It occurs in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, that they should not fear nor grieve." Abu al-Aliya said: "Do not fear regarding what you have done, and do not grieve over what you have left behind." Mujahid said: "Do not fear what you are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind in your worldly life of family, children, and offspring, for We shall replace you in all of that." Al-Suddi said: "Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you." Ata ibn Rabah said: "Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them for you."

The people of language said regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ with fidelity to abandoning harshness, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ with contentment, ﴿saying: Do not fear﴾ hardship, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over perishing, ﴿and rejoice in the Garden with which you were promised﴾ in meeting. "Do not fear," for there is no fear upon the people of steadfastness; "do not grieve," for you have all kinds of honour; "and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of safety." Do not fear, for you have held fast to the religion of Allah; do not grieve, for you have held fast to the rope of Allah; and rejoice in the Garden, even if you were doubtful and grieved. Do not grieve, for you have long been fearful; do not grieve, for you have attained what you sought; and rejoice in the Garden, in which you desired. Do not fear, for you are the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are the people of forgiveness; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of good pleasure. Do not fear, for you are the people of martyrdom; do not grieve, for you are the people of felicity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of increase. Do not fear, for you are the people of gifts; do not grieve, for you are the people of union; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of majesty. Do not fear, for you are safe from destruction; do not grieve, for the time of joy has come to you; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of delight. Do not fear, for your effort is appreciated; do not grieve, for your sin is forgiven; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of... Do not fear, for you have long been among the fearful; do not grieve, for you have been among the knowers; and rejoice in the Garden, which the describers cannot describe. Do not fear, for there is no fear upon the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are not among the deprived; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of faith. Do not fear, for you are not among the people of Hellfire; do not grieve, for you have reached the Lord, the Merciful; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of bliss. Do not fear, for fear has been removed from you; do not grieve, for you have been saved from every calamity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of hospitality. Do not grieve over removal from authority; do not grieve over what you have previously done of betrayal; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of guidance. Do not fear the descent of punishment; do not grieve over the terror of the reckoning; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of reward. Do not fear, for you are safe from punishment; do not grieve, for you will reach reward; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is an excellent return. Do not fear, for you are the people of fidelity; do not grieve over what you have earned of harshness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of purity. Do not fear, for you are safe from ruin; do not grieve, for you have been saved from weariness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of delight.

﴿We are your allies﴾

The angels who descend upon them with glad tidings say: ﴿We are your allies﴾, your helpers and your friends, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We are your allies﴾ means: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world," and ﴿We are your allies...in the Hereafter.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ibn Khalid informed us, Dawud ibn Amr al-Dabbi informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "They are their companions who were with them in the world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will say: 'We will not leave you until we bring you into the Garden.'"

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾, that is, what you wish, request, and wish for. The original phrase is: whatever you claim is yours, it is yours by the judgment of your Lord.

﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾: that is, this was made as provision. ﴿From One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And they say, meaning the disbelievers who are gathered to the Fire: ﴿To their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "Allah, who made everything speak, has made us speak."﴾

Aqil ibn Muhammad related to us: Abu al-Faraj al-Baghdadi al-Qadi informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, Shurayk informed us, from Ubayd al-Makit, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day until his molars showed, then said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?"

They said: "What did you laugh at, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "I was amazed at the servant's dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says, 'O Lord, did You not promise that You would not wrong me?' He says, 'Indeed.' He says, 'Then I accept no witness against myself except my own self.' He says, 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do."

He said: "Then he will say to them, 'Away with you! Perish! It was on your behalf that I was disputing.'" [161] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 7/55.]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you, but you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ That is, "you were not concealing yourselves" means you were hiding yourselves, according to the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "you were fearing (taqun)." Qatada said: "you were thinking."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun and Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Warraq related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir and Abu Hudhayfa related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Umara ibn Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men came: a man from Thaqif and two sons-in-law from Quraysh. Their bellies were full of fat, and their understanding was little. They spoke among themselves, and one of them said, 'Do you think He hears what we say?' The other said, 'If we raise our voices He hears, and if we lower them He does not hear.' Another said, 'If He hears when we raise our voices, then He hears when we lower them.' So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him of that, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And you were not concealing yourselves, lest your hearing and your sights and your skins should testify against you...﴾ up to His words: ﴿...you became among the losers.﴾"

The Thaqafi was Abd Yalil, and his two sons-in-law from Quraysh were Rabi'a and Safwan ibn Umayya.

﴿And that was your thinking, which you thought of your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾ "Destroyed you" means caused you to perish. Qatada said: "Here, 'thinking' means knowledge."

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Let none of you die except while thinking well of Allah, for a people who thought ill of their Lord were destroyed by it." That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And that was your thinking...﴾ the verse. [162] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/353.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim al-Nahawandi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us, Ahmad ibn Hafs related to us, my father related to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted says: "I am according to My servant's thought of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me." [163] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 4/412.]]

Qatada said: "Whoever among you is able to die while thinking well of his Lord, let him do so, for thinking is of two kinds: a thought that saves, and a thought that destroys." Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Bahili said:

"The one who thinks well is at rest;
the one whose thought is ugly is distressed.
From the Spirit of Allah, in every direction
winds have blown upon him.
The man does not fail of a gift of generosity;
only the miser perishes."

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode; and if they seek to be pleased, they will not be among those who are pleased.﴾ "They seek to be pleased" means they ask to be reconciled and seek reconciliation. "Those who are pleased" means those who are accepted, and al-mu'tabb is one whose reproach is accepted and who is granted what he asks. Ubayd ibn Umayr recited ﴿wa in tusta'tabu﴾ in the passive form, and ﴿fa-ma hum mina al-mu'tabin﴾ with a kasra on the ta'. The meaning is: if they ask to do what would please their Lord, ﴿they are not among those who are pleased﴾, that is, they are not able to please their Lord, because they have left the abode of action.

﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: We empowered, sent, and assigned. ﴿Companions﴾: counterparts, from among the devils. ﴿And they made fair to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter; ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection.

﴿And the word has come true against them﴾ along with nations ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and men. Indeed they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾ from among the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: That means "drown it out," that some of them would instruct others: "When you see Muhammad reciting, oppose him with shouting and turning away." Mujahid said: ﴿make noise during it﴾ means with whistling and clapping, and confusion in speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recited. Al-Dahhak said: "Speak much, so that his words become confused." Al-Suddi said: "Shout in his face." Muqatil said: "Raise your voices with poetry and talk in their faces until you confuse their recitation, and they fall silent." Abu al-Aliya said: "Find fault with it and disparage it."

Isa ibn Amr recited ﴿al-ghu fihi﴾ with a damma on the ghayn. Al-Akhfash said: the fatha on the ghayn comes from laghiya yalghā, like taghā yatghā; and whoever puts a damma on the ghayn, from laghā yalghū, like da'ā yad'ū.

﴿So that you may overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what they used to do.﴾ "The worst" means the most abominable. ﴿What they used to do﴾ in this world. ﴿That﴾ is what you have been told of. ﴿Is the recompense of the enemies of Allah.﴾ Then He explained what that recompense is: ﴿The Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity, a recompense for what they used to deny Our signs.﴾ It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Abbas it reads: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," where "the abode" is used to refer to the Fire, which is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse.

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "Our Lord, show us the two who led us astray from among the jinn,"﴾ which is Iblis and the devils, ﴿and mankind,﴾ which is the son of Adam who killed his brother. ﴿We will place them beneath our feet in the Fire, so that they may be among the lowest.﴾ In the lowest abyss, because they were the originators of disobedience.

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Zaydi al-Askari informed us, Amr ibn Ali related to us, Abu Qutayba Salama ibn Qutayba related to us, Sahl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding his words, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "Whoever dies upon it is among those who have remained steadfast." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 5/54.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Thaqafi informed us, with my reading to him: Ubayd ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba related to us, Ja'far ibn al-Farabi related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Balkhi related to us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿then remain steadfast﴾: "They did not associate anything with Allah."

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Thaqafi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, my father related to us, Uthman ibn Umar related to us, Yunus related to us, from al-Zuhri, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), while delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit, recited ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "They remained steadfast upon the way of Allah by obeying Him, then did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "That means they made their action sincerely for Allah."

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They performed the obligatory duties."

Ibn Abbas: "They remained steadfast in performing His obligations."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Halwani related to us, Isma'il ibn Bishr ibn Mansur related to us, Miskin Abu Fatima related to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Al-Hasan said, reciting this verse, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾: "They remained steadfast upon the command of Allah, acting in obedience to Him and avoiding His disobedience." Mujahid and Ikrima said: "They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah, until they met Him." Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: "They remained steadfast in the worship and obedience of Allah." Ibn Sirin said: "They did not deviate." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "They acted in accordance with what they said." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They remained steadfast upon knowledge and did not apostatize." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "They remained steadfast upon the fact that Allah is their Lord." Al-Rabi' said: "They turned away from all besides Allah the Exalted." Fudayl ibn Iyad said: "They renounced the perishable and desired the enduring." Some of them said: "They remained steadfast in secret as they remained steadfast in declaration." It was also said: "They remained steadfast in deed as they remained steadfast in word."

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said when this verse was revealed: "My community, and by the Lord of the Ka'ba." [164] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/358.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sunni related to us, both saying: Abu Khalifa al-Fadl ibn Hayyan al-Jumahi related to us, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a matter to hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then remain steadfast." I said: "What is the thing you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took hold of his own tongue and said: "This." [165] [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/413.]]

It is also narrated that a delegation came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he recited the Qur'an to them, then wept. They said: "Do you weep out of fear of the One who sent you?" He said: "Yes. I have been sent upon a path like the edge of a sword: if I remain steadfast I am saved, and if I swerve from it I am destroyed." [166] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/201, with variation.]]

Qatada said: "When al-Hasan recited this verse, he would say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

﴿The angels descend upon them﴾ at the time of death, ﴿saying, "Do not fear and do not grieve."﴾ Qatada said: "When they rise from their graves." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah al-Basri said: "It occurs in three situations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, that they should not fear nor grieve." Abu al-Aliya said: "Do not fear regarding what you have done, and do not grieve over what you have left behind." Mujahid said: "Do not fear what you are going to face of the affairs of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind in your worldly life of family, children, and offspring, for We shall replace you in all of that." Al-Suddi said: "Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you." Ata ibn Rabah said: "Do not fear and do not grieve over your sins, for I will forgive them for you."

The people of language said regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remain steadfast﴾ with fidelity to abandoning harshness, ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ with contentment, ﴿saying: Do not fear﴾ hardship, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over perishing, ﴿and rejoice in the Garden with which you were promised﴾ in meeting. "Do not fear," for there is no fear upon the people of steadfastness; "do not grieve," for you have all kinds of honour; "and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of safety." Do not fear, for you have held fast to the religion of Allah; do not grieve, for you have held fast to the rope of Allah; and rejoice in the Garden, even if you were doubtful and grieved. Do not grieve, for you have long been fearful; do not grieve, for you have attained what you sought; and rejoice in the Garden, in which you desired. Do not fear, for you are the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are the people of forgiveness; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of good pleasure. Do not fear, for you are the people of martyrdom; do not grieve, for you are the people of felicity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of increase. Do not fear, for you are the people of gifts; do not grieve, for you are the people of union; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of majesty. Do not fear, for you are safe from destruction; do not grieve, for the time of joy has come to you; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of delight. Do not fear, for your effort is appreciated; do not grieve, for your sin is forgiven; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of... Do not fear, for you have long been among the fearful; do not grieve, for you have been among the knowers; and rejoice in the Garden, which the describers cannot describe. Do not fear, for there is no fear upon the people of faith; do not grieve, for you are not among the deprived; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of faith. Do not fear, for you are not among the people of Hellfire; do not grieve, for you have reached the Lord, the Merciful; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of bliss. Do not fear, for fear has been removed from you; do not grieve, for you have been saved from every calamity; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of hospitality. Do not grieve over removal from authority; do not grieve over what you have previously done of betrayal; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of guidance. Do not fear the descent of punishment; do not grieve over the terror of the reckoning; and rejoice in the Garden, which is the abode of reward. Do not fear, for you are safe from punishment; do not grieve, for you will reach reward; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is an excellent return. Do not fear, for you are the people of fidelity; do not grieve over what you have earned of harshness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of purity.
