Do not fear, for you are safe from ruin; do not grieve, for you have been saved from weariness; and rejoice in the Garden, for it is the abode of delight.

﴿We are your allies﴾

The angels who descend upon them with glad tidings say: ﴿We are your allies﴾, your helpers and your friends, ﴿in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾

Al-Suddi said: ﴿We are your allies﴾ means: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world," and ﴿We are your allies...in the Hereafter.﴾

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, Ibn Khalid informed us, Dawud ibn Amr al-Dabbi informed us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath informed us, from al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "They are their companions who were with them in the world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will say: 'We will not leave you until we bring you into the Garden.'"

﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾, that is, what you wish, request, and wish for. The original phrase is: whatever you claim is yours, it is yours by the judgment of your Lord.

﴿As a hospitable welcome﴾: that is, this was made as provision. ﴿From One who is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 41, verse 33–54:

﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, to obedience to Allah, and does righteous deeds, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ Ibn Sirin, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: he is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Muqatil said: he is all the imams and those who call to Allah, exalted is He. Ikrimah said: he is the muezzin (mu'adhdhin). Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: "and does righteous deeds" means he prays two rak'ahs between the adhan and the iqamah.

Ibn Hamid informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn Yarham ibn Sufyan told us: Abdullah ibn Hashim told us: Waki' told us: Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi told us, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "I believe this verse was revealed concerning the muezzins: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah...﴾ the verse."

Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated from Fudayl ibn Rufaydah, who said: "I was a muezzin in the time of the companions of Abdullah. Asim ibn Hubayrah said to me: 'When you call the adhan and finish your adhan, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, and I am of the Muslims. Then recite this verse: ﴿And good and evil are not equal...﴾'" Al-Farra' said:

"Wa la (and not) here is a connecting particle (silah); its meaning is: ﴿and good and evil are not equal﴾," and he recited:

"What pleased the Messenger of Allah was not their deed, / and the two good ones, Abu Bakr and Umar."

That is, Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).

﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Close friend. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, who used to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but then became his friend after having been an enemy. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will create affection between you and those of them with whom you have enmity﴾ [60:7]. Ibn Abbas said: In this verse Allah commands patience at anger, forbearance at ignorance, and pardon at offence. When they do that, Allah protects them from Satan, and their enemy submits to them, ﴿as though he were a devoted friend.﴾

﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ "It" means this quality and this act: in goodness and reward. It was said: "one of fortune." ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾ Hearing your seeking refuge and your words; Knowing your deeds and your states.

﴿And of His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.﴾ He said "khalaqahunna" (created them, feminine) because it was treated as a broken plural (jam' taksir), and not in the manner of giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine, since it refers to non-rational things. ﴿But if they are arrogant, [it does not matter], for those who are near your Lord,﴾ meaning the angels, ﴿exalt Him by night and day, and they do not tire.﴾

This is based on His saying: ﴿They are not too arrogant to worship Him, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾ [7:206].

﴿And of His signs is that you see the earth humbled; but when We send down upon it water, it quivers and grows.﴾ Dry, withered, without vegetation. ﴿Indeed, He who brought it to life is the Giver of life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾ — that is, who incline away from the truth in Our proofs.

Ibn Abbas said: it is altering speech and placing it in other than its proper place. Mujahid said: ﴿deviate concerning Our signs﴾ by whistling, clapping, idle talk and noise. Qatadah: it means they lie concerning Our signs. Al-Suddi: they obstinately oppose and dissent. Ibn Zayd: they associate partners with Allah and deny. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him.

﴿They are not hidden from Us. So is one who is thrown into the Fire [better] or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ — Abu Jahl is the first, and the second is Uthman ibn Affan. It was also said: Ammar ibn Yasir. ﴿Do as you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ A command of warning and threat. Indeed, He is Knower, and will recompense you for it.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them [will not be hidden from Us]﴾ — the Reminder: the Qur'an; when it came to them: at the time it came to them. ﴿And indeed, it is a Mighty Book﴾ — honoured with Allah; this is from Ibn Abbas. Muqatil said: protected from Satan and falsehood. Al-Suddi: uncreated.

﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it﴾ — Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this means Satan; so he cannot change it, add to it, or subtract from it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means denunciation does not reach it. It was also said: no book comes after it to nullify or abrogate it, nor does anything that refutes or nullifies it come from earlier scriptures; rather it agrees with them and confirms them. Transmitted from al-Kalbi. ﴿A revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you.﴾ He consoles His Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the harm said to him. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for whoever repents, and the Possessor of painful punishment for whoever persists.﴾

﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: "Why are its verses not explained clearly?"﴾ — that is, made clear in our language, so that we may understand it; for we are an Arab people, what have we to do with the non-Arabic? ﴿Is it [a Book] non-Arabic and [a messenger] Arab?﴾ — meaning: a non-Arabic book and an Arab prophet?

Muqatil said: this is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to visit Yasar, the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami, who was a non-Arab Jew and was called Abu Fukayhah. The polytheists said: "It is only Yasar who teaches him." So his master Amir ibn al-Hadrami seized him and beat him, saying: "You teach Muhammad!" Yasar said: "He teaches me." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan recited: "a'jami" with a single hamzah, as a statement; and Hisham narrated the same from the people of Syria.

Its basis is what Ja'far ibn al-Mughirah narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Quraysh said: "Why was this Qur'an not revealed non-Arabic and Arabic, so that some of its verses are non-Arabic and some Arabic?" So Allah revealed this verse, and the Qur'an was revealed in every language: among it is "sijjil," which is Persian, arabized as "sang" and "gil." The correct reading, however, is the reading of the majority, with the interrogative, according to the first interpretation.

﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is for them blindness.﴾ Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us: Hajjaj ibn Ayyub told us, from Shu'bah, from Musa ibn Abi Aishah, from Salman ibn Qutaybah, from Ibn Abbas, Mu'awiyah and Amr ibn al-As, that they used to read these words with a kasrah on the mim: "wa huwa 'alayhim 'ami" (and it is for them blindness). The rest read with a fathah on the mim, as a verbal noun (masdar), and Abu Ubayd chose this. He said: because of His saying "guidance and healing," which are verbal nouns similar to it; if it were "hadin" and "shafin" (active participles), the kasrah on "ami" would be better, so that it would be an adjective like them.

﴿Those are called from a distant place.﴾ Some of the scholars of meaning said: His saying "Those are called from a distant place" is the predicate of His saying "Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them." Al-Tabari narrated, saying: a shaykh of the people of knowledge told me: "I heard Isa ibn Umar ask Amr ibn Ubayd: 'Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them — where is its predicate?' Amr said: 'Its meaning in exegesis is: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them disbelieved in it, and indeed it is a Mighty Book.' Isa ibn Umar said: 'You have done well, Abu Uthman.'"

As for His saying, exalted is He, "They are called from a distant place," it is an analogy: as though their listening and benefiting from what they are admonished with is distant, as if they are called to faith and to the Qur'an from a place they cannot hear from because of the great distance.

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but it came to be disputed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them.﴾ Some believed in it and some disbelieved, some confirmed and some denied, just as your people disputed your Book. "If not for a word" — concerning the delay of the punishment; "it would have been judged between them" — of their punishment, and their destruction would have been hastened. ﴿And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾

﴿Whoever does righteousness does so for himself, and whoever does evil does so against himself. And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾ — for none knows it but Him.

This is because the polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you are a prophet, inform us when the Hour will be established; and if you do not know that, then you are not a prophet." So Allah revealed this verse.

﴿Not does any fruit emerge from its sheaths﴾ — "min" here is connected to "thamarat" (fruits). With the plural, the people of Madinah and Syria read it; others read "thamarah" in the singular. ﴿from its sheaths (akmam)⌋ — its containers; its singular is "kimmah," which is every container for property or other things; and likewise the spathe of the date palm (kafra) is called "kimmah," meaning the sheath that splits open to release the fruit. Ibn Abbas said: it means the kafra before it splits; when it has split, it is no longer a sheath. ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge.﴾ He says: to Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour, just as the knowledge of fruits and offspring is referred to Him.

﴿And the day He will call them: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ — meaning Allah, exalted is He, calls the polytheists. ﴿They will say: "We have informed You; none of us is a witness."﴾ "They" means the polytheists; it was also said: the idols; it is possible that the speech refers both to the worshippers and to the worshipped. "We have informed You" — we have made You know; it was also said: "We have made You hear." ﴿None of us is a witness﴾ — a witness that You have a partner. When they witnessed the Resurrection, they disowned the idols, and the idols disowned them. ﴿And lost from them is what they used to invoke before﴾ — in the world.

﴿And they will be certain﴾ — they will be certain, ﴿that there is for them no place of escape﴾ — no refuge. Here "ma" is a particle, not a noun, so "zanna" (to think/suppose) does not operate on it, and the verb is left suspended (mulqa).

﴿Man does not tire of invoking good﴾ — "yasam" means to grow weary; "al-insan" means the disbeliever. ﴿of [asking for] good﴾ — that is, of his supplication for good and his asking his Lord. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Abdullah: "la yas'amu al-insanu min du'a'i al-khayr," meaning: for health and wealth. ﴿But if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless﴾ — despairing of the mercy of Allah. ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after hardship had touched him﴾ — health and blessing; ﴿hardship had touched him﴾ — distress and affliction that befell him. ﴿He will surely say, "This is mine,"﴾ — by my own deeds, and I deserve this.

﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever occur. And if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward].﴾ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan told us: Abdullah ibn Thabit told us: Abu Sa'id al-Kindi told us: Ahmad ibn Bishr told us, from Abu Shurmah, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali Abi Talib, who said:

"The disbeliever has two wishes. In this world he says: '[And if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best].' And in the Hereafter he says: 'Would that I had been dust.'"

..

﴿So We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ — harsh.

﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ — abundant. The Arabs use both "length" and "breadth" to express abundance; it is said: "So-and-so lengthened his speech and supplication," and "a'rada" when he increases.

﴿Say: "Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾ ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: meaning the dwellings of the former nations. ﴿And within themselves﴾ — through affliction and diseases. Al-Minhal and al-Suddi said: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means what is opened to Muhammad (ﷺ) of the horizons; ﴿within themselves﴾ means Makkah. Qatadah said: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means the events of Allah among the nations; ﴿within themselves﴾ means the Day of Badr.

Ata' and Ibn Zayd: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means the regions of the earth and the heavens: the sun, the moon, the stars, the plants, the trees, the rivers, the seas and the rains; ﴿within themselves﴾ means the subtle craftsmanship and wondrous wisdom, and the passages of the excrement and urine, so that a man eats and drinks from one place, and what he eats and drinks exits from two places.

﴿Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.﴾ That is, what We show them and do of that is the truth. It was said: it means Islam; it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ); it was said: the Qur'an. ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt over the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is, of all things, Encompassing.﴾

Asim ibn Hubayrah said to me: 'When you call the adhan and finish your adhan, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, and I am of the Muslims. Then recite this verse: ﴿And good and evil are not equal...﴾'" Al-Farra' said:

"What pleased the Messenger of Allah was not their deed, / and the two good ones, Abu Bakr and Umar."

That is, Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).

﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Close friend. ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: "Why are its verses not explained clearly?"﴾ — that is, made clear in our language, so that we may understand it; for we are an Arab people, what have we to do with the non-Arabic? ﴿Is it [a Book] non-Arabic and [a messenger] Arab?﴾ — meaning: a non-Arabic book and an Arab prophet?

Muqatil said: this is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to visit Yasar, the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami, who was a non-Arab Jew and was called Abu Fukayhah. The polytheists said: "It is only Yasar who teaches him." So his master Amir ibn al-Hadrami seized him and beat him, saying: "You teach Muhammad!" Yasar said: "He teaches me." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan recited: "a'jami" with a single hamzah, as a statement; and Hisham narrated the same from the people of Syria.

Its basis is what Ja'far ibn al-Mughirah narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Quraysh said: "Why was this Qur'an not revealed non-Arabic and Arabic, so that some of its verses are non-Arabic and some Arabic?" So Allah revealed this verse, and the Qur'an was revealed in every language: among it is "sijjil," which is Persian, arabized as "sang" and "gil." The correct reading, however, is the reading of the majority, with the interrogative, according to the first interpretation.

﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is for them blindness.﴾ Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub informed us: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us: Hajjaj ibn Ayyub told us, from Shu'bah, from Musa ibn Abi Aishah, from Salman ibn Qutaybah, from Ibn Abbas, Mu'awiyah and Amr ibn al-As, that they used to read these words with a kasrah on the mim: "wa huwa 'alayhim 'ami" (and it is for them blindness). The rest read with a fathah on the mim, as a verbal noun (masdar), and Abu Ubayd chose this. He said: because of His saying "guidance and healing," which are verbal nouns similar to it; if it were "hadin" and "shafin" (active participles), the kasrah on "ami" would be better, so that it would be an adjective like them.

﴿Those are called from a distant place.﴾ Some of the scholars of meaning said: His saying "Those are called from a distant place" is the predicate of His saying "Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them." Al-Tabari narrated, saying: a shaykh of the people of knowledge told me: "I heard Isa ibn Umar ask Amr ibn Ubayd: 'Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them — where is its predicate?' Amr said: 'Its meaning in exegesis is: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them disbelieved in it, and indeed it is a Mighty Book.' Isa ibn Umar said: 'You have done well, Abu Uthman.'"

As for His saying, exalted is He, "They are called from a distant place," it is an analogy: as though their listening and benefiting from what they are admonished with is distant, as if they are called to faith and to the Qur'an from a place they cannot hear from because of the great distance.

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but it came to be disputed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them.﴾ Some believed in it and some disbelieved, some confirmed and some denied, just as your people disputed your Book. "If not for a word" — concerning the delay of the punishment; "it would have been judged between them" — of their punishment, and their destruction would have been hastened. ﴿And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾

﴿Whoever does righteousness does so for himself, and whoever does evil does so against himself. And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾ — for none knows it but Him.

This is because the polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you are a prophet, inform us when the Hour will be established; and if you do not know that, then you are not a prophet." So Allah revealed this verse.

﴿Not does any fruit emerge from its sheaths﴾ — "min" here is connected to "thamarat" (fruits). With the plural, the people of Madinah and Syria read it; others read "thamarah" in the singular. ﴿from its sheaths (akmam)⌋ — its containers; its singular is "kimmah," which is every container for property or other things; and likewise the spathe of the date palm (kafra) is called "kimmah," meaning the sheath that splits open to release the fruit. Ibn Abbas said: it means the kafra before it splits; when it has split, it is no longer a sheath. ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge.﴾ He says: to Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour, just as the knowledge of fruits and offspring is referred to Him.

﴿And the day He will call them: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ — meaning Allah, exalted is He, calls the polytheists. ﴿They will say: "We have informed You; none of us is a witness."﴾ "They" means the polytheists; it was also said: the idols; it is possible that the speech refers both to the worshippers and to the worshipped. "We have informed You" — we have made You know; it was also said: "We have made You hear." ﴿None of us is a witness﴾ — a witness that You have a partner. When they witnessed the Resurrection, they disowned the idols, and the idols disowned them. ﴿And lost from them is what they used to invoke before﴾ — in the world.

﴿And they will be certain﴾ — they will be certain, ﴿that there is for them no place of escape﴾ — no refuge. Here "ma" is a particle, not a noun, so "zanna" (to think/suppose) does not operate on it, and the verb is left suspended (mulqa).

﴿Man does not tire of invoking good﴾ — "yasam" means to grow weary; "al-insan" means the disbeliever. ﴿of [asking for] good﴾ — that is, of his supplication for good and his asking his Lord. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Abdullah: "la yas'amu al-insanu min du'a'i al-khayr," meaning: for health and wealth. ﴿But if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless﴾ — despairing of the mercy of Allah. ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after hardship had touched him﴾ — health and blessing; ﴿hardship had touched him﴾ — distress and affliction that befell him. ﴿He will surely say, "This is mine,"﴾ — by my own deeds, and I deserve this.

﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever occur. And if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward].﴾ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan told us: Abdullah ibn Thabit told us: Abu Sa'id al-Kindi told us: Ahmad ibn Bishr told us, from Abu Shurmah, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali Abi Talib, who said:

"The disbeliever has two wishes. In this world he says: '[And if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best].' And in the Hereafter he says: 'Would that I had been dust.'"

..

﴿So We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ — harsh.

﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ — abundant. The Arabs use both "length" and "breadth" to express abundance; it is said: "So-and-so lengthened his speech and supplication," and "a'rada" when he increases.

﴿Say: "Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾ ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: meaning the dwellings of the former nations. ﴿And within themselves﴾ — through affliction and diseases. Al-Minhal and al-Suddi said: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means what is opened to Muhammad (ﷺ) of the horizons; ﴿within themselves﴾ means Makkah. Qatadah said: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means the events of Allah among the nations; ﴿within themselves﴾ means the Day of Badr.

Ata' and Ibn Zayd: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means the regions of the earth and the heavens: the sun, the moon, the stars, the plants, the trees, the rivers, the seas and the rains; ﴿within themselves﴾ means the subtle craftsmanship and wondrous wisdom, and the passages of the excrement and urine, so that a man eats and drinks from one place, and what he eats and drinks exits from two places.

﴿Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.﴾ That is, what We show them and do of that is the truth. It was said: it means Islam; it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ); it was said: the Qur'an. ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt over the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is, of all things, Encompassing.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 41, verse 33–54:

﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, to obedience to Allah, and does righteous deeds, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ Ibn Sirin, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: he is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Muqatil said: he is all the imams and those who call to Allah, exalted is He. Ikrimah said: he is the muezzin (mu'adhdhin). Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: "and does righteous deeds" means he prays two rak'ahs between the adhan and the iqamah.

Ibn Hamid informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn Yarham ibn Sufyan told us: Abdullah ibn Hashim told us: Waki' told us: Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi told us, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "I believe this verse was revealed concerning the muezzins: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah...﴾ the verse."

Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated from Fudayl ibn Rufaydah, who said: "I was a muezzin in the time of the companions of Abdullah. Asim ibn Hubayrah said to me: 'When you call the adhan and finish your adhan, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, and I am of the Muslims. Then recite this verse: ﴿And good and evil are not equal...﴾'" Al-Farra' said:

"Wa la (and not) here is a connecting particle (silah); its meaning is: ﴿and good and evil are not equal﴾," and he recited:

"What pleased the Messenger of Allah was not their deed, / and the two good ones, Abu Bakr and Umar."

That is, Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).

﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Close friend. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, who used to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but then became his friend after having been an enemy. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will create affection between you and those of them with whom you have enmity﴾ [60:7]. Ibn Abbas said: In this verse Allah commands patience at anger, forbearance at ignorance, and pardon at offence. When they do that, Allah protects them from Satan, and their enemy submits to them, ﴿as though he were a devoted friend.﴾

﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ "It" means this quality and this act: in goodness and reward. It was said: "one of fortune." ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾ Hearing your seeking refuge and your words; Knowing your deeds and your states.

﴿And of His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.﴾ He said "khalaqahunna" (created them, feminine) because it was treated as a broken plural (jam' taksir), and not in the manner of giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine, since it refers to non-rational things. ﴿But if they are arrogant, [it does not matter], for those who are near your Lord,﴾ meaning the angels, ﴿exalt Him by night and day, and they do not tire.﴾

This is based on His saying: ﴿They are not too arrogant to worship Him, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾ [7:206].

﴿And of His signs is that you see the earth humbled; but when We send down upon it water, it quivers and grows.﴾ Dry, withered, without vegetation. ﴿Indeed, He who brought it to life is the Giver of life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾ — that is, who incline away from the truth in Our proofs.

Ibn Abbas said: it is altering speech and placing it in other than its proper place. Mujahid said: ﴿deviate concerning Our signs﴾ by whistling, clapping, idle talk and noise. Qatadah: it means they lie concerning Our signs. Al-Suddi: they obstinately oppose and dissent. Ibn Zayd: they associate partners with Allah and deny. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him.

﴿They are not hidden from Us. So is one who is thrown into the Fire [better] or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ — Abu Jahl is the first, and the second is Uthman ibn Affan. It was also said: Ammar ibn Yasir. ﴿Do as you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ A command of warning and threat. Indeed, He is Knower, and will recompense you for it.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them [will not be hidden from Us]﴾ — the Reminder: the Qur'an; when it came to them: at the time it came to them. ﴿And indeed, it is a Mighty Book﴾ — honoured with Allah; this is from Ibn Abbas. Muqatil said: protected from Satan and falsehood. Al-Suddi: uncreated.

﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it﴾ — Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this means Satan; so he cannot change it, add to it, or subtract from it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means denunciation does not reach it. It was also said: no book comes after it to nullify or abrogate it, nor does anything that refutes or nullifies it come from earlier scriptures; rather it agrees with them and confirms them. The rest read with a fathah on the mim, as a verbal noun (masdar), and Abu Ubayd chose this. He said: because of His saying "guidance and healing," which are verbal nouns similar to it; if it were "hadin" and "shafin" (active participles), the kasrah on "ami" would be better, so that it would be an adjective like them.

﴿Those are called from a distant place.﴾ Some of the scholars of meaning said: His saying "Those are called from a distant place" is the predicate of His saying "Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them." Al-Tabari narrated, saying: a shaykh of the people of knowledge told me: "I heard Isa ibn Umar ask Amr ibn Ubayd: 'Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them — where is its predicate?' Amr said: 'Its meaning in exegesis is: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them disbelieved in it, and indeed it is a Mighty Book.' Isa ibn Umar said: 'You have done well, Abu Uthman.'"

As for His saying, exalted is He, "They are called from a distant place," it is an analogy: as though their listening and benefiting from what they are admonished with is distant, as if they are called to faith and to the Qur'an from a place they cannot hear from because of the great distance.

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but it came to be disputed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them.﴾ Some believed in it and some disbelieved, some confirmed and some denied, just as your people disputed your Book. "If not for a word" — concerning the delay of the punishment; "it would have been judged between them" — of their punishment, and their destruction would have been hastened. ﴿And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾

﴿Whoever does righteousness does so for himself, and whoever does evil does so against himself. And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾ — for none knows it but Him.

This is because the polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you are a prophet, inform us when the Hour will be established; and if you do not know that, then you are not a prophet." So Allah revealed this verse.

﴿Not does any fruit emerge from its sheaths﴾ — "min" here is connected to "thamarat" (fruits). With the plural, the people of Madinah and Syria read it; others read "thamarah" in the singular. ﴿from its sheaths (akmam)⌋ — its containers; its singular is "kimmah," which is every container for property or other things; and likewise the spathe of the date palm (kafra) is called "kimmah," meaning the sheath that splits open to release the fruit. Ibn Abbas said: it means the kafra before it splits; when it has split, it is no longer a sheath. ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge.﴾ He says: to Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour, just as the knowledge of fruits and offspring is referred to Him.

﴿And the day He will call them: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ — meaning Allah, exalted is He, calls the polytheists. ﴿They will say: "We have informed You; none of us is a witness."﴾ "They" means the polytheists; it was also said: the idols; it is possible that the speech refers both to the worshippers and to the worshipped. "We have informed You" — we have made You know; it was also said: "We have made You hear." ﴿None of us is a witness﴾ — a witness that You have a partner. When they witnessed the Resurrection, they disowned the idols, and the idols disowned them. ﴿And lost from them is what they used to invoke before﴾ — in the world.

﴿And they will be certain﴾ — they will be certain, ﴿that there is for them no place of escape﴾ — no refuge. Here "ma" is a particle, not a noun, so "zanna" (to think/suppose) does not operate on it, and the verb is left suspended (mulqa).

﴿Man does not tire of invoking good﴾ — "yasam" means to grow weary; "al-insan" means the disbeliever. ﴿of [asking for] good﴾ — that is, of his supplication for good and his asking his Lord. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Abdullah: "la yas'amu al-insanu min du'a'i al-khayr," meaning: for health and wealth. ﴿But if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless﴾ — despairing of the mercy of Allah. ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after hardship had touched him﴾ — health and blessing; ﴿hardship had touched him﴾ — distress and affliction that befell him. ﴿He will surely say, "This is mine,"﴾ — by my own deeds, and I deserve this.

﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever occur. And if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward].﴾ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan told us: Abdullah ibn Thabit told us: Abu Sa'id al-Kindi told us: Ahmad ibn Bishr told us, from Abu Shurmah, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali Abi Talib, who said:

"The disbeliever has two wishes. In this world he says: '[And if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best].' And in the Hereafter he says: 'Would that I had been dust.'"

﴿So We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ — harsh.

﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and distances himself; but when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾ — abundant. The Arabs use both "length" and "breadth" to express abundance; it is said: "So-and-so lengthened his speech and supplication," and "a'rada" when he increases.

﴿Say: "Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾ ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons﴾ — Ibn Abbas said: meaning the dwellings of the former nations. ﴿And within themselves﴾ — through affliction and diseases. Al-Minhal and al-Suddi said: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means what is opened to Muhammad (ﷺ) of the horizons; ﴿within themselves﴾ means Makkah. Qatadah said: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means the events of Allah among the nations; ﴿within themselves﴾ means the Day of Badr.

Ata' and Ibn Zayd: ﴿in the horizons﴾ means the regions of the earth and the heavens: the sun, the moon, the stars, the plants, the trees, the rivers, the seas and the rains; ﴿within themselves﴾ means the subtle craftsmanship and wondrous wisdom, and the passages of the excrement and urine, so that a man eats and drinks from one place, and what he eats and drinks exits from two places.

﴿Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.﴾ That is, what We show them and do of that is the truth. It was said: it means Islam; it was said: Muhammad (ﷺ); it was said: the Qur'an. ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt over the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is, of all things, Encompassing.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 41, verse 33–54:

﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, to obedience to Allah, and does righteous deeds, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ Ibn Sirin, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: he is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Muqatil said: he is all the imams and those who call to Allah, exalted is He. Ikrimah said: he is the muezzin (mu'adhdhin). Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: "and does righteous deeds" means he prays two rak'ahs between the adhan and the iqamah.

Ibn Hamid informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn Yarham ibn Sufyan told us: Abdullah ibn Hashim told us: Waki' told us: Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi told us, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "I believe this verse was revealed concerning the muezzins: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah...﴾ the verse."

Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated from Fudayl ibn Rufaydah, who said: "I was a muezzin in the time of the companions of Abdullah. Asim ibn Hubayrah said to me: 'When you call the adhan and finish your adhan, say: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, and I am of the Muslims. Then recite this verse: ﴿And good and evil are not equal...﴾'" Al-Farra' said:

"Wa la (and not) here is a connecting particle (silah); its meaning is: ﴿and good and evil are not equal﴾," and he recited:

"What pleased the Messenger of Allah was not their deed, / and the two good ones, Abu Bakr and Umar."

That is, Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both).

﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Close friend. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, who used to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but then became his friend after having been an enemy. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿It may be that Allah will create affection between you and those of them with whom you have enmity﴾ [60:7]. Ibn Abbas said: In this verse Allah commands patience at anger, forbearance at ignorance, and pardon at offence. When they do that, Allah protects them from Satan, and their enemy submits to them, ﴿as though he were a devoted friend.﴾

﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ "It" means this quality and this act: in goodness and reward. It was said: "one of fortune." ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾ Hearing your seeking refuge and your words; Knowing your deeds and your states.

﴿And of His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him you worship.﴾ He said "khalaqahunna" (created them, feminine) because it was treated as a broken plural (jam' taksir), and not in the manner of giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine, since it refers to non-rational things. ﴿But if they are arrogant, [it does not matter], for those who are near your Lord,﴾ meaning the angels, ﴿exalt Him by night and day, and they do not tire.﴾

This is based on His saying: ﴿They are not too arrogant to worship Him, and they exalt Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾ [7:206].

﴿And of His signs is that you see the earth humbled; but when We send down upon it water, it quivers and grows.﴾ Dry, withered, without vegetation. ﴿Indeed, He who brought it to life is the Giver of life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾ — that is, who incline away from the truth in Our proofs.

Ibn Abbas said: it is altering speech and placing it in other than its proper place. Mujahid said: ﴿deviate concerning Our signs﴾ by whistling, clapping, idle talk and noise. Qatadah: it means they lie concerning Our signs. Al-Suddi: they obstinately oppose and dissent. Ibn Zayd: they associate partners with Allah and deny. Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him.

﴿They are not hidden from Us. So is one who is thrown into the Fire [better] or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ — Abu Jahl is the first, and the second is Uthman ibn Affan. It was also said: Ammar ibn Yasir. ﴿Do as you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ A command of warning and threat. Indeed, He is Knower, and will recompense you for it.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them [will not be hidden from Us]﴾ — the Reminder: the Qur'an; when it came to them: at the time it came to them. ﴿And indeed, it is a Mighty Book﴾ — honoured with Allah; this is from Ibn Abbas. Muqatil said: protected from Satan and falsehood. Al-Suddi: uncreated.

﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it﴾ — Qatadah and al-Suddi said: this means Satan; so he cannot change it, add to it, or subtract from it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means denunciation does not reach it. It was also said: no book comes after it to nullify or abrogate it, nor does anything that refutes or nullifies it come from earlier scriptures; rather it agrees with them and confirms them. Transmitted from al-Kalbi. ﴿A revelation from One Wise, Praiseworthy.﴾

﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you.﴾ He consoles His Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the harm said to him. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for whoever repents, and the Possessor of painful punishment for whoever persists.﴾

﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said: "Why are its verses not explained clearly?"﴾ — that is, made clear in our language, so that we may understand it; for we are an Arab people, what have we to do with the non-Arabic? ﴿Is it [a Book] non-Arabic and [a messenger] Arab?﴾ — meaning: a non-Arabic book and an Arab prophet?

Muqatil said: this is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to visit Yasar, the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami, who was a non-Arab Jew and was called Abu Fukayhah. The polytheists said: "It is only Yasar who teaches him." So his master Amir ibn al-Hadrami seized him and beat him, saying: "You teach Muhammad!" Yasar said: "He teaches me." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan recited: "a'jami" with a single hamzah, as a statement; and Hisham narrated the same from the people of Syria.

Its basis is what Ja'far ibn al-Mughirah narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Quraysh said: "Why was this Qur'an not revealed non-Arabic and Arabic, so that some of its verses are non-Arabic and some Arabic?" So Allah revealed this verse, and the Qur'an was revealed in every language: among it is "sijjil," which is Persian, arabized as "sang" and "gil." The correct reading, however, is the reading of the majority, with the interrogative, according to the first interpretation.
